topics_covered.title: 1.1 Congress of Vienna (1815), Industrial Capitalism, Socialism, and Labor Movements
topics_covered.topic_title: 1.1 Congress of Vienna (1815), Industrial Capitalism, Socialism, and Labor Movements
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Metternich’s Concert of Europe, legitimacy and balance of power, Chartism, Utopian vs Scientific Socialism (Marxism), and the Paris Commune.

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.
topics_covered.explanation: Global modern history connects industrialization, world wars, ideological Cold War rivalry, and the triumph of African decolonization and continental integration.

topics_covered.title: 1.1 Congress of Vienna (1815), Industrial Capitalism, Socialism, and Labor Movements
topics_covered.topic_title: 1.1 Congress of Vienna (1815), Industrial Capitalism, Socialism, and Labor Movements
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Metternich’s Concert of Europe, legitimacy and balance of power, Chartism, Utopian vs Scientific Socialism (Marxism), and the Paris Commune.

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Mazzini’s Young Italy, Piedmont-Sardinia diplomacy, Garibaldi’s Red Shirts, Zollverein, and Bismarck’s three wars (Denmark, Austria 1866, France 1870–71).

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

topics_covered.topic_title: 1.3 The American Civil War (1861–65), Meiji Restoration in Japan, and the Eastern Question
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Abraham Lincoln, Emancipation Proclamation (1863), abolition of slavery (13th Amendment), Japanese industrial modernization, and Ottoman Balkan crises.

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

book-12-soc-hist_ch_1_topic_congress_of_.detailed_overview:
Global modern history connects industrialization, world wars, ideological Cold War rivalry, and the triumph of African decolonization and continental integration.

Key Takeaway: Bismarck unified Germany and chaired the 1884 Berlin Conference; Addis Ababa hosted the 1963 founding of the OAU uniting Africa.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Addis Ababa serves as the diplomatic capital of Africa, hosting the permanent headquarters of the OAU (since 1963), the African Union (AU), and the UN Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA).

topics_covered.title: 1.1 Congress of Vienna (1815), Industrial Capitalism, Socialism, and Labor Movements
topics_covered.topic_title: 1.1 Congress of Vienna (1815), Industrial Capitalism, Socialism, and Labor Movements
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Metternich’s Concert of Europe, legitimacy and balance of power, Chartism, Utopian vs Scientific Socialism (Marxism), and the Paris Commune.

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Global modern history connects industrialization, world wars, ideological Cold War rivalry, and the triumph of African decolonization and continental integration.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Metternich’s Concert of Europe, legitimacy and balance of power, Chartism, Utopian vs Scientific Socialism (Marxism), and the Paris Commune.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
- **Key Principle**: British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
- **Key Principle**: The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

topics_covered.topic_title: 1.1 Congress of Vienna (1815), Industrial Capitalism, Socialism, and Labor Movements
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Metternich’s Concert of Europe, legitimacy and balance of power, Chartism, Utopian vs Scientific Socialism (Marxism), and the Paris Commune.

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Global modern history connects industrialization, world wars, ideological Cold War rivalry, and the triumph of African decolonization and continental integration.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Mazzini’s Young Italy, Piedmont-Sardinia diplomacy, Garibaldi’s Red Shirts, Zollverein, and Bismarck’s three wars (Denmark, Austria 1866, France 1870–71).

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
- **Key Principle**: British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
- **Key Principle**: The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Continental Integration Path: [1958 Accra All-African Peoples Conference] ──> [Casablanca vs Monrovia Blocs] ──> [May 25, 1963 OAU Charter in Addis Ababa] ──> [2002 African Union (AU) & Agenda 2063].
```

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Mazzini’s Young Italy, Piedmont-Sardinia diplomacy, Garibaldi’s Red Shirts, Zollverein, and Bismarck’s three wars (Denmark, Austria 1866, France 1870–71).

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).

The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

topics_covered.topic_title: 2.1 The Scramble for Africa, Berlin Conference (1884–85), and Effective Occupation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: King Leopold II in Congo, Fashoda Incident (1898), Articles 34 & 35 of the Berlin Act, and geometric boundary demarcation.

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

topics_covered.topic_title: 2.2 African Anti-Colonial Resistance: Samori Ture, Ashanti, Maji-Maji, Mahdist & Urabi
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Mandinka Empire scorched-earth tactics, Yaa Asantewaa, Kinjikitile Ngwale’s Maji-Maji uprising (1905–07), and Herero-Nama resistance.

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

book-12-soc-hist_ch_2_topic_the_scramble.detailed_overview:
Global modern history connects industrialization, world wars, ideological Cold War rivalry, and the triumph of African decolonization and continental integration.

Key Takeaway: Bismarck unified Germany and chaired the 1884 Berlin Conference; Addis Ababa hosted the 1963 founding of the OAU uniting Africa.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Addis Ababa serves as the diplomatic capital of Africa, hosting the permanent headquarters of the OAU (since 1963), the African Union (AU), and the UN Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA).

topics_covered.title: 2.1 The Scramble for Africa, Berlin Conference (1884–85), and Effective Occupation
topics_covered.topic_title: 2.1 The Scramble for Africa, Berlin Conference (1884–85), and Effective Occupation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: King Leopold II in Congo, Fashoda Incident (1898), Articles 34 & 35 of the Berlin Act, and geometric boundary demarcation.

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

book-12-soc-hist_ch_2_The Scramble for A.detailed_overview:
Global modern history connects industrialization, world wars, ideological Cold War rivalry, and the triumph of African decolonization and continental integration.

Key Takeaway: Bismarck unified Germany and chaired the 1884 Berlin Conference; Addis Ababa hosted the 1963 founding of the OAU uniting Africa.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Addis Ababa serves as the diplomatic capital of Africa, hosting the permanent headquarters of the OAU (since 1963), the African Union (AU), and the UN Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA).

topics_covered.title: 2.1 The Scramble for Africa, Berlin Conference (1884–85), and Effective Occupation
topics_covered.topic_title: 2.1 The Scramble for Africa, Berlin Conference (1884–85), and Effective Occupation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: King Leopold II in Congo, Fashoda Incident (1898), Articles 34 & 35 of the Berlin Act, and geometric boundary demarcation.

• Industrial Revolution, Nationalism & Imperialism: Industrial Revolution began in Britain (steam engine, factory mechanization, coal/iron). Unification of Italy (1861–1870: Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini) and Germany (1871: Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Franco-Prussian War). Berlin Conference (1884–85, chaired by Bismarck) formalized the "Effective Occupation" doctrine for the Scramble for Africa.

• World War I & Interwar Crisis (1914–1939): Alliances: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) vs. Triple Alliance/Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). Sparked by June 28, 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. 1917 Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Lenin). Treaty of Versailles (1919) and League of Nations. 1929 Great Depression and rise of Fascism (Mussolini) and Nazism (Hitler).

• World War II & The Cold War (1939–1991): WWII (1939–1945): Axis Powers vs. Allied Powers (turning points: Stalingrad, Midway, El Alamein, Normandy D-Day). Creation of the United Nations (1945: UN Security Council with 5 permanent veto powers: US, USSR/Russia, UK, France, China). Cold War ideological bipolarity: US Capitalism (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO 1949) vs. Soviet Communism (Warsaw Pact 1955), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung 1955).

• Pan-Africanism, Decolonization & OAU/AU: Pan-African Congresses (W.E.B. Du Bois, Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie). Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (1957). Organization of African Unity (OAU) founded in Addis Ababa on May 25, 1963 (Casablanca vs. Monrovia blocs reconciled by Emperor Haile Selassie); transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002 (Durban). End of Apartheid in South Africa (1994, Nelson Mandela).
key_points: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).
British colonial rule typically used Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), whereas French colonial rule used Assimilation and Association.
The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

Global modern history connects industrialization, world wars, ideological Cold War rivalry, and the triumph of African decolonization and continental integration.

- **Key Principle**: At the 1963 OAU founding summit in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie bridged the radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah - immediate political federation) and moderate Monrovia Group (gradual functional cooperation).

- **Key Principle**: The Cold War was termed "cold" because the two nuclear superpowers (USA and USSR) never engaged in direct full-scale military combat against each other, fighting instead via proxy wars.

Global modern history connects industrialization, world wars, ideological Cold War rivalry, and the triumph of African decolonization and continental integration.
